name: send-to-peer-repo
query: send a message to the agent in ~/dev/raziel asking for its schema
why: The canonical send: a named peer repo and a request. If this misses, the skill has no reason to exist.

name: check-my-inbox
why: The boot rule in the user's own words. Ambiguous against human mail in principle, but 'my inbox' in an agent repo means the agent-root inbox.

name: any-mail-from-peers
query: did the other agent send anything back
why: Receiving side with no inbox or mail vocabulary. Checks the trigger reads inter-agent intent rather than a keyword.

name: hand-off-to-another-repo
query: hand this task off to whoever owns the frontend repo
why: A handoff-type message across repo boundaries. No send or message verb, which is the point.

name: reply-to-a-message
query: reply to that request from the peer agent and mark it resolved
why: The response leg plus mark.sh closure. Names the two steps the skill insists never get hand-edited.

name: notify-peer-of-a-change
query: let the agent that owns the API repo know we changed the contract
why: An fyi-type message. The verb is notify, not send, and the recipient is another repo's agent.

name: inbox-outstanding
query: is anything still outstanding in the inbox
why: The closing sweep rather than the listing. Distinguishing the two is the skill's own rule.

name: human-email-client
query: email the client a status update on the migration
why: Human email. No skill here; the agent drafts or sends through whatever mail tooling the user has. Agent-mail writes markdown files into a peer repo and never reaches a person's mailbox.

name: human-email-inbox
query: check my email, did anything come in from the vendor
why: Human email. The hardest false case: same verb and same noun as the boot rule, but a named human counterparty settles it.

name: draft-an-email
query: draft an email to the vendor about the invoice
why: Human email. Prose for a person, with no recipient repo and no inbox folder.

name: human-chat-message
query: message the team on Slack that the deploy is done
why: Human chat. Message and notify are agent-mail verbs, but the channel is a person-facing one.

name: subagent-prompt
query: spawn a subagent and tell it to audit the config files
why: The Agent tool, or cover-me if the intent is review. A subagent receives a prompt at spawn and has no inbox; mail is between independent agents that outlive a turn.

name: github-issue-comment
query: post a comment on the GitHub issue so the other team sees it
why: The gh CLI. Cross-team communication through a hosted tracker, not a same-machine file drop into a peer repo.
